title: Impeccable
summary: The missing design vocabulary for agents: commands to build, review and refine UI, plus a detector for AI slop.

sections.title: Modes
sections.intro: Chosen per surface: what does the visitor’s success look like?

items.title: Persuade
items.text: Landing, marketing, pricing.

items.title: Operate
items.text: App UI, dashboards, settings.

items.title: Read
items.text: Docs, articles, guides.

items.title: Experience
items.text: Portfolios, galleries.
items.more: The artifact leads, the interface recedes.

items.title: Measure
items.text: Body text at 45–75 characters per line.

items.title: Display limits
items.text: Display max 6rem; tracking floor -0.04em, -0.02 to -0.03em usually reads better.

items.title: Obvious steps
items.text: Heading, body, label and data roles distinguishable at a glance.

items.title: Earn every family
items.text: Faces and weights should fit the product, not be unexamined defaults.

items.title: Stress test
items.text: Long headings, localization, zoom, narrow containers, font fallback.

items.title: Real display face
items.text: Not a system face like Impact or Arial Black as the display voice.

items.title: Contrast
items.text: Body 4.5:1, large text 3:1, controls and focus 3:1.

items.title: Tinted secondary text
items.text: On colored surfaces tint from the hue; never gray.

items.title: Rarity gives force
items.text: In Operate and Read, color encodes action, status and wayfinding.

items.title: Not color alone
items.text: Pair color with text, shape, icon or position.

items.title: OKLCH ramps
items.text: Vary lightness, reduce chroma near white and black.

items.title: Explicit over alpha
items.text: Translucent overlay chains make contrast unpredictable.

items.title: Rhythm
items.text: Tight groups, generous separation.

items.title: Headings
items.text: More space above a heading than below.

items.title: Squint test
items.text: Blurred, you can still find primary, secondary and groups.

items.title: Proximity over containers
items.text: Containers shouldn’t compensate for weak grouping.

items.title: Fit the content
items.text: Repeated cards only when items are truly equivalent.

items.title: 100–150 ms
items.text: Immediate feedback

items.title: 150–300 ms
items.text: Routine state change

items.title: 300–500 ms
items.text: Layout, overlay or view transition

items.title: 500–800 ms
items.text: A deliberately authored focal entrance

items.title: One authored moment
items.text: Not the same entrance on every section.

items.title: Ease out
items.text: Exit faster than entrance; no reflexive bounce or elastic.

items.title: Every state
items.text: Hover, disabled, loading, error, empty, keyboard focus.

items.title: Browser surfaces
items.text: Theme selection, caret, scrollbars, focus rings, tabular numerals.

items.title: No needless modals
items.text: Only when a task needs interruption or protected focus.

items.title: Undo over confirm
items.text: When recovery is safe, prefer undo.

items.title: Assess context
items.text: Device, input, screen, connection, usage, expectations.

items.title: Touch targets
items.text: 44×44px minimum, more spacing between controls.

items.title: No hover-only
items.text: Remove hover-dependent interactions on touch.

items.title: Fluid tools
items.text: Grid and flexbox, container queries, clamp().

items.title: Order agrees
items.text: DOM and focus order match the visual order.

items.title: Verb + object
items.text: Labels say what will happen, not the gesture.

items.title: Consistent nouns
items.text: Same verb and noun for the same concept everywhere.

items.title: Name the action
items.text: Not Yes, No, OK or Submit on confirmations.

items.title: Persistent labels
items.text: Placeholders are examples, not labels.

items.title: Actionable errors
items.text: What failed, why, and how to recover.

sections.title: Anti-patterns
sections.intro: From the craft floor. Defaults to refuse unless the brief earns them; eyebrows are an outright ban.
items: Same-size icon + heading + text cards as page structure
Eyebrow or kicker above a heading
Modal for a task that doesn’t need one
Sparklines and rings standing in for content
System display face as the display voice
Emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons
Light or dark picked by category
Border plus wide soft shadow: the ghost card

overview.purpose: Design vocabulary for coding agents: commands to build, review and refine UI.

takeaways: Critique and audit before you refine
